name: Interactive Task and Concept Learning from Natural Language Instructions and GUI Demonstrations
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot.
summary: Introduces PUMICE, an agent that learns mobile-app procedures and conditional concepts through natural-language conversation and GUI demonstrations, recursively resolving ambiguous instructions with users.

name: Mobile App Tasks with Iterative Feedback (MoTIF): Addressing Task Feasibility in Interactive Visual Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces MoTIF, a dataset of natural-language requests for interactive mobile apps, including infeasible requests and follow-up questions for studying task feasibility.

name: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The browser interaction serves long-form question answering, evaluated on ELI5.
summary: Trains a question-answering model to search and navigate a text-based web browser, collect references and improve long-form answers using demonstrations and human feedback.

name: A Dataset for Interactive Vision-Language Navigation with Unknown Command Feasibility
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces MoTIF mobile-app interactions with feasible and infeasible commands, feasibility explanations, and follow-up questions for ambiguous requests.

name: META-GUI: Towards Multi-modal Conversational Agents on Mobile GUI
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI-based task-oriented dialogue and a dataset pairing mobile-interface operations with conversational responses.

name: MUG: Interactive Multimodal Grounding on User Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies iterative UI grounding in which users refine or correct an agent's interpretation over multiple conversational turns.

name: UINav: A Practical Approach to Train On-Device Automation Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4).
summary: Introduces UINav, a demonstration-based method for training mobile UI automation agents, with a referee model for failure feedback and automatic augmentation of examples.

name: MobileAgent: enhancing mobile control via human-machine interaction and SOP integration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines operating-procedure context with user interaction to guide mobile task automation and handle personalized or sensitive requests.

name: GPTVoiceTasker: Advancing Multi-step Mobile Task Efficiency Through Dynamic Interface Exploration and Learning
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces GPTVoiceTasker, a mobile assistant that interprets user commands, executes device interactions, and learns from prior commands to streamline later task execution. The work includes a user study of task efficiency.

name: Prompt2Task: Automating UI Tasks on Smartphones from Textual Prompts
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Prompt2Task converts textual goals or procedures into smartphone UI automation using agents for intent interpretation, external-information handling, and execution. User feedback and accumulated task knowledge support subsequent task generation and operation.

name: FlowMind: Automatic Workflow Generation with LLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: FlowMind generates API-based workflows from user requests for process automation and presents workflow descriptions that users can inspect and comment on.

name: Unveiling Disparities in Web Task Handling Between Human and Web Agent
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Compares human think-aloud web-task behavior with web-agent planning, action, and reflection. The analysis highlights differences in updating plans, handling ambiguity, and investigating failures.

name: VLM Agents Generate Their Own Memories: Distilling Experience into Embodied Programs of Thought
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v6). VisualWebArena is one of several evaluation settings for this general VLM-agent method.
summary: ICAL turns imperfect agent trajectories into reusable strategies and action annotations through reflection and human feedback, with VisualWebArena among its evaluations.

name: IDA: Breaking Barriers in No-code UI Automation Through Large Language Models and Human-Centric Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: IDA helps business users create web UI automation through guided demonstrations, a semantic programming model, and a teaching-oriented interface. A prototype user study examines automation creation with enterprise applications by users without programming backgrounds.

name: Interactive Speculative Planning: Enhance Agent Efficiency through Co-design of System and User Interface
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies agent-system and interface co-design that incorporates user interruptions and intermediate feedback to reduce planning latency.

publication.date_basis: The ACL Anthology citation_publication_date is 2025/4, and its visible Month/Year fields state April 2025. Only month precision is supplied; no day is inferred from conference dates.

This attaches the proceedings edition to the existing arXiv identity.
publication.notes: The April 2025 proceedings edition is distinct from the retained arXiv v4, last revised on 2026-02-27. The publisher abstract has minor wording and typesetting differences from the retained arXiv abstract; neither its text nor its date replaces the original arXiv snapshot or annotation. Exact publication day, numeric volume, issue and series are not established.
publication.title: CowPilot: A Framework for Autonomous and Human-Agent Collaborative Web Navigation
publication.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (System Demonstrations)

name: CowPilot: A Framework for Autonomous and Human-Agent Collaborative Web Navigation
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.
summary: Introduces CowPilot, a web-navigation framework where agents suggest actions and users can pause, reject, override, or resume them. It evaluates autonomous and collaborative use through task success and human effort.

name: COLA: A Scalable Multi-Agent Framework For Windows UI Task Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Coordinates specialized Windows UI agents with dynamic task scheduling, shared memory, and human-triggered rollback for recovering from errors.

name: Towards Computer-Using Personal Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Proposes computer-using personal agents connected to user-controlled data repositories, discussing privacy, interoperability, and collaborative tasks.

name: OS-Kairos: Adaptive Interaction for MLLM-Powered GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses step-level confidence estimates to decide when a GUI agent should act autonomously or request human intervention in complex situations.

name: Agent-Initiated Interaction in Phone UI Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Defines when phone agents should request user interaction and introduces AndroidInteraction annotations for deciding whether and how to engage the user.

name: Navi-plus: Managing Ambiguous GUI Navigation Tasks with Follow-up Questions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Navi-plus evaluates GUI agents that ask follow-up questions to complete ambiguous user instructions. It provides GUI clarification question-answer pairs and Dual-Stream Trajectory Evaluation for this interactive setting.

name: RealWebAssist: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Web Assistance with Real-World Users
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RealWebAssist evaluates web assistance through sequences of instructions collected from real users across multiple websites. It tests intent interpretation, user-specific routines, long-term context, and visual grounding when instructions are ambiguous or evolve during interaction.

name: The Obvious Invisible Threat: LLM-Powered GUI Agents' Vulnerability to Fine-Print Injections
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Characterizes six forms of GUI-content injection and studies their effects on GUI agents and human users using adversarial webpages. The analysis examines privacy failures and the limits of human oversight.

name: LearnAct: Few-Shot Mobile GUI Agent with a Unified Demonstration Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LearnAct parses human demonstrations into reusable knowledge, retrieves relevant examples, and uses them during mobile GUI task execution. The accompanying LearnGUI benchmark includes 2,252 offline tasks and 101 online tasks for studying adaptation from demonstrations.

name: Toward a Human-Centered Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy LLM-Powered GUI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. This is a position paper proposing an evaluation framework; the abstract does not report a new benchmark or empirical validation of the proposed framework.
summary: Presents a position paper on privacy and security evaluation for GUI agents, identifying risk categories and challenges in involving human evaluators. It proposes risk-aware assessment and in-context consent as design directions.

name: Characterizing Unintended Consequences in Human-GUI Agent Collaboration for Web Browsing
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies unintended consequences of collaborative web browsing with GUI agents through social-media analysis and interviews. It organizes observed failures, user impacts, and mitigation practices around planning, interface interaction, feedback, privacy, and trust.

name: Creating General User Models from Computer Use
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Proposes general user models that turn computer-use observations into confidence-weighted propositions and revise them as new context arrives. Demonstrations use this memory to contextualize assistants, manage notifications, and support proactive actions across apps.

name: Mobile-Bench-v2: A More Realistic and Comprehensive Benchmark for VLM-based Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Mobile-Bench-v2 evaluates mobile GUI agents using multiple acceptable offline action paths, noisy interfaces with ads or pop-ups, and ambiguous instructions with scripted clarification exchanges. These splits separate step-level execution, robustness, and proactive interaction.

name: VerificAgent: Domain-Specific Memory Verification for Scalable Oversight of Aligned Computer-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces VerificAgent, which grows domain-specific memories from task trajectories and subjects them to human fact-checking before deployment. Its OSWorld evaluation treats persistent memory as an auditable constraint on later agent behavior.

name: ProactiveVA: Proactive Visual Analytics with LLM-Based UI Agent
notes: Adjacent work on embedded assistance in two instrumented visual-analytics systems. Its in-lab user-study evidence is context-specific, and the paper discusses clarification and intervention-control trade-offs. General GUI-agent performance is not inferred. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (5.3 User study; 5.3.2 Observed issues; 6.1 Design trade-off; 6.2 Limitations).
summary: Studies proactive assistance in visual-analytics interfaces, using interaction logs to detect support needs and provide context-aware suggestions and guidance.

name: Magentic-UI: Towards Human-in-the-loop Agentic Systems
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Magentic-UI combines browser interaction, code execution, file operations, and MCP tools in an interface for human-agent collaboration. It studies collaborative planning and task execution, action guards, and persistent memory through benchmark tasks, simulated users, user studies, and safety assessments.

name: Uncertainty-Aware GUI Agent: Adaptive Perception through Component Recommendation and Human-in-the-Loop Refinement
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RecAgent narrows attention to recommended UI components and requests user feedback when task intent or decisions remain uncertain. It introduces ComplexAction to evaluate specified single-step GUI actions in difficult interface scenarios.

name: MVISU-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents for Real-World Tasks by Multi-App, Vague, Interactive, Single-App and Unethical Instructions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MVISU-Bench evaluates bilingual mobile tasks involving cross-app work, vague requests, user interaction and unethical instructions alongside ordinary single-app tasks. Its Aider prompting module is designed to clarify intent and mitigate risky execution within agent workflows.

name: PerPilot: Personalizing VLM-based Mobile Agents via Memory and Exploration
notes: Personalization depends on the validity of stored or inferred user information and retrieval access. This is instruction completion with interaction, not demonstrated permanent model-weight personalization. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (The Framework of PerPilot; Personalization Perception; Personalization Completion; PerInstruct Data Construction).
summary: Introduces PerPilot and the PerInstruct dataset for completing user-specific mobile instructions through memory retrieval, app exploration, and clarification when missing context remains unresolved.

name: InquireMobile: Teaching VLM-based Mobile Agent to Request Human Assistance via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: InquireMobile trains mobile agents to seek human confirmation at critical decisions using staged reinforcement fine-tuning and pre-action reasoning. InquireBench evaluates safe interaction and proactive inquiry, distinguishing asking for help from completing the underlying task.

name: Morae: Proactively Pausing UI Agents for User Choices
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.
summary: Introduces Morae, a UI agent that detects decision points and pauses for user choices using interface code and screenshots. A study with blind and low-vision participants evaluates this mixed-initiative approach on real web tasks.

name: VeriOS: Query-Driven Proactive Human-Agent-GUI Interaction for Trustworthy OS Agents
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.
summary: Introduces VeriOS-Agent, which learns when to execute GUI actions autonomously and when to query a user under untrustworthy conditions. Its staged training combines supervised learning and group-relative policy optimization.

name: Dark Patterns Meet GUI Agents: LLM Agent Susceptibility to Manipulative Interfaces and the Role of Human Oversight
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies how GUI agents, people, and human-agent teams respond to manipulative interface designs. The two-phase evaluation examines failure modes and the benefits and costs of human oversight.

name: PrivWeb: Unobtrusive and Content-aware Privacy Protection For Web Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces PrivWeb, which uses a local language model to anonymize interface information according to user preferences. Adaptive notifications and selective pauses give users control over sensitive information access during web-agent tasks.

name: Robust, Observable, and Evolvable Agentic Systems Engineering: A Principled Framework Validated via the Fairy GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents an agent-engineering framework combining runtime goal clarification, an observable component architecture and evolving execution memory. The Fairy mobile GUI agent evaluates these mechanisms on ambiguous tasks and through controlled and user studies.

name: BrowserArena: Evaluating LLM Agents on Real-World Web Navigation Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces BrowserArena, a live-web platform for head-to-head agent comparisons on user-submitted tasks. Step-level human annotations support targeted analysis of navigation, pop-up handling and CAPTCHA-related failures.

name: Understanding User Experiences of Computer Use Agents: Design Space and Opportunities for Building Agent UX Prototypes
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). AgentUXlab prototypes agent experiences for a website and runs them in a browser.
summary: Maps design considerations for computer-use agent experiences and introduces AgentUXlab, a browser-based probe for prototyping and evaluating agent UX on a website.

name: ReInAgent: A Context-Aware GUI Agent Enabling Human-in-the-Loop Mobile Task Navigation
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces ReInAgent, coordinating information management, planning, and reflection around a shared memory for mobile tasks. It proactively asks users for information and checks consistency when instructions are ambiguous or change during execution.

name: ALLOY: Generating Reusable Agent Workflows from User Demonstration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The study involved 12 participants performing complex web tasks.
summary: Introduces ALLOY, which turns user demonstrations into editable, reusable workflows for LLM-based web agents carrying out preference-dependent tasks.

name: State Your Intention to Steer Your Attention: An AI Assistant for Intentional Digital Living
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces an assistant that reads screenshots, application titles, and URLs to compare computer activity with a user's stated intention and send notifications when it diverges.

name: ColorAgent: Building A Robust, Personalized, and Interactive OS Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract says current benchmarks are insufficient for comprehensive evaluation of OS agents.
summary: Presents ColorAgent, an operating system agent for long-horizon user instructions, trained with step-wise RL and self-evolving training and evaluated on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.

name: DrawingBench: Evaluating Spatial Reasoning and UI Interaction Capabilities of Large Language Models through Mouse-Based Drawing Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: DrawingBench evaluates sequences of low-level mouse-based GUI actions through 250 drawing prompts and rule-based criteria. Action inspection and multi-turn external feedback support analysis of spatial reasoning, tool-state management, and refinement.

name: LegalWebAgent: Empowering Access to Justice via LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LegalWebAgent separates user-needs clarification, webpage browsing, and actions such as form completion or scheduling. A 15-task evaluation studies legal-service workflows relevant to Québec civil-law users, using HTML and screenshot observations.

name: MAI-UI Technical Report: Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: MAI-UI combines GUI navigation, native user interaction, and MCP tool calls in a family of policies trained through generated data and online reinforcement learning. The report also studies device-cloud routing and scaling of parallel environments and interaction budgets, with grounding and Android navigation evaluation.

name: ColorBrowserAgent: Complex Long-Horizon Browser Agent with Adaptive Knowledge Evolution
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ColorBrowserAgent converts human feedback into reusable website knowledge and uses that knowledge to guide progressive context summaries. It evaluates the resulting memory and adaptation mechanisms on long browser workflows.

name: The Behavioral Fabric of LLM-Powered GUI Agents: Human Values and Interaction Outcomes
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces a controlled web-task testbed for studying how stated preferences and human values influence GUI-agent decisions. It analyzes how personas alter navigation and how prominent interface cues can override the intended preference guidance.

name: From Struggle to Success: Context-Aware Guidance for Screen Reader Users in Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AskEase, an on-demand assistant that combines contextual information to provide screen-reader-friendly computer-use guidance. A study with screen-reader users evaluates task completion and perceived workload while preserving human control of the interaction.

name: OS-Marathon: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents on Vast-Horizon, Repetitive Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces OS-Marathon to evaluate long repetitive computer-use workflows whose execution grows with the amount of input data. It studies failure accumulation under task decomposition and GraphDemo, which adapts agents using a demonstration of the recurring workflow.

name: Mapping the Design Space of User Experience for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Develops a taxonomy of computer-use-agent interaction design through system review and practitioner interviews. A Wizard-of-Oz study then examines how users respond to normal, erroneous, and risky web-based execution, focusing on control, explanation, prompts, and mental models.

name: A11y-CUA Dataset: Characterizing the Accessibility Gap in Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces A11y-CUA, a dataset comparing how blind or low-vision users and sighted users perform everyday computer tasks. It contrasts those traces with agent behavior under default, keyboard-only, and magnifier conditions to identify barriers to shared control.

name: LHAW: Controllable Underspecification for Long-Horizon Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: LHAW generates underspecified variants of long-horizon workflow tasks and uses agent trials to evaluate when missing information requires clarification.

name: AmbiBench: Benchmarking Mobile GUI Agents Beyond One-Shot Instructions in the Wild
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AmbiBench evaluates mobile GUI agents under four levels of instruction clarity, including tasks requiring active clarification. Its MUSE evaluator separately audits outcomes, execution quality and interaction quality to study alignment with user intent.

name: Modeling Distinct Human Interaction in Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CowCorpus records interleaved human and agent actions during web navigation and identifies distinct patterns of user intervention. Models trained to anticipate these interventions are integrated into live web agents and assessed in a user study.

name: PIRA-Bench: A Transition from Reactive GUI Agents to GUI-based Proactive Intent Recommendation Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: PIRA-Bench evaluates proactive intent recommendations from noisy GUI screenshot sequences containing interleaved tasks and user context. Its PIRF baseline combines memory and state tracking to maintain multiple task threads and identify opportunities to assist.

name: Terminal Is All You Need: Design Properties for Human-AI Agent Collaboration
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent conceptual HCI work about agent-facing interfaces; the abstract does not report GUI task experiments or a new evaluated CUA.
summary: This position paper derives interface design principles from terminal-based human-agent collaboration: representational compatibility, transparent actions and low participation barriers. It argues that graphical and other agent-facing modalities should provide these properties explicitly.

name: IntentWeave: A Progressive Entry Ladder for Multi-Surface Browser Agents in Cloud Portals
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The prototype and user study are set on a single cloud website.
summary: Introduces IntentWeave, a design space and browser-extension prototype for placing web-agent assistance across browser surfaces, evaluated through a study of three entry strategies.

name: GUIDE: A Benchmark for Understanding and Assisting Users in Open-Ended GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUIDE evaluates whether models can recognize a user’s behavior, infer intent and decide when to offer help during open-ended software tasks. It uses narrated screen recordings of novice users and studies the effect of additional user context on these assistance decisions.

name: When Users Change Their Mind: Evaluating Interruptible Agents in Long-Horizon Web Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Interruptions are evaluated through synthesized scenarios in a simulation framework.
summary: Introduces InterruptBench, a WebArena-Lite-derived benchmark that tests how long-horizon web-navigation agents handle mid-task user additions, revisions, and retractions.

name: Comparing Human Oversight Strategies for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Compares four human oversight strategies during live web-agent sessions, examining exposure to problematic actions and opportunities to intervene. The analysis identifies timing and attention problems in control handoffs and upfront plan approval.

name: MAESTRO: Adapting GUIs and Guiding Navigation with User Preferences in Conversational Agents with GUIs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces MAESTRO, a conversational GUI system that remembers user preferences, adapts interface options, and guides backtracking in multistep booking decisions.

name: KnowU-Bench: Towards Interactive, Proactive, and Personalized Mobile Agent Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces KnowU-Bench, an Android emulator benchmark for mobile agents that evaluates preference elicitation, proactive decisions, consent and GUI task execution.

name: Agentic Compilation: Mitigating the LLM Rerun Crisis for Minimized-Inference-Cost Web Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports evaluation on data extraction, form filling, and fingerprinting tasks.
summary: Proposes Compile-and-Execute, which turns a sanitized DOM into a reusable JSON workflow so repetitive browser tasks can run without further model queries.

name: Beyond Chat and Clicks: GUI Agents for In-Situ Assistance via Live Interface Transformation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: DOMSteer translates help requests and live page context into reversible DOM changes such as control highlighting, contextual tooltips and layout reorganization. The work evaluates in-place GUI assistance with interface tests, use cases and a comparative user study.

name: AgentClick: A Skill-Based Human-in-the-Loop Review Layer for Terminal AI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent supervision interface: the browser UI is for human review of terminal agents; the abstract does not claim that those agents operate graphical interfaces.
summary: AgentClick gives terminal-based agents a browser review interface for plans, drafts, execution traces and editable memory. A local server and skill plugin let users inspect proposed actions and provide structured feedback.

name: Human-Guided Harm Recovery for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports human evaluation of recovery trajectories produced by the proposed scaffold.
summary: Introduces a preference-trained reward model for guiding computer-use agents out of harmful states and BackBench, a benchmark of recovery tasks.

name: AgentLens: Adaptive Visual Modalities for Human-Agent Interaction in Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). Its reported user findings come from a controlled study with 21 participants.
summary: Introduces AgentLens, a mobile GUI agent that shows full, partial, or generated interface views during background task execution to support user interaction.

name: PageGuide: Browser extension to assist users in navigating a webpage and locating information
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v5). PageGuide assists users with navigation and verification; the abstract reports a user study.
summary: PageGuide is a browser extension that highlights evidence for answers on a page and guides users through web pages with evidence captured at each step.

name: Mobile-Aptus: Confidence-Driven Proactive and Robust Interaction in MLLM-based Mobile-Using Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Mobile-Aptus trains mobile agents to output actions and confidence scores, then corrects confidence bias to guide when they request human help.

name: MaskClaw: Edge-Side Personalized Privacy Arbitration for GUI Agents with Behavior-Driven Skill Evolution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MaskClaw makes local Allow, Mask or Ask decisions before GUI screenshots leave a trusted environment, using visual evidence and personalized policy memory. Its benchmark and designed evolution scenarios test how corrections and edits can become privacy skills checked by a sandbox gate.

name: DeskCraft: Benchmarking Desktop Agents on Professional Workflows and Human-in-the-Loop Collaboration
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DeskCraft evaluates professional desktop workflows and human-agent collaboration through mid-execution clarification, interruption and post-completion feedback. Its tasks cover creative applications and expose difficulties in long-horizon execution and proactive clarification.

name: Syll: Open-Source Personal Automation with Cross-Surface Execution
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Syll combines tool calls, shell execution and visual GUI control in a personal-automation runtime. It turns user demonstrations into reusable skills and exposes execution logs, keyframes and approval checkpoints for inspection.

name: HANSEL: Extracting Breadcrumbs from Web Agent Trajectories for Interactive Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: HANSEL extracts evidence pages and snippets from browser-agent traces and preserves relevant page state in interactive verification views. It flags untraceable answers and evaluates evidence selection and human verification effort separately.

name: GUI agent: Guided Exploration of User-Sensitive Screens
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: This short paper develops an explorer agent that expands from a demonstrated GUI task to discover requests likely to reach user-sensitive screens. The proposed exploration supports identifying situations where task execution should be handed back to the user.

name: DigitalCoach: Communication and Grounding Gaps in Human and Agentic Computer Use Coaching
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: DigitalCoach records expert–novice software coaching conversations aligned with screen and input events. Automated and interactive evaluations examine how model coaches differ from humans in explanation, error diagnosis and visual grounding when helping a learner operate software.

name: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces UniClawBench, a benchmark of proactive agents on bilingual real-world tasks, evaluated in live Docker containers with stepwise checkpoints and simulated user feedback.

name: Plover: Steering GUI Agents through Plan-Centric Interaction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Plover exposes GUI-agent plans and replanning as persistent artifacts that users can inspect and edit during execution. Its planner–executor design supports localized correction through plan edits, language guidance and screenshot-grounded interventions, studied through failure repair and workflow scenarios.

name: Just A Rather Very Intelligent Spoken Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces JarvisBench, a benchmark for spoken mediation during long-horizon agent workflows, measuring task collaboration and how users follow ongoing execution.

name: Sidekick: Designing Communication for Effective Multitasking with Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Sidekick, a communication interface that uses ambient status cues, multimodal action summaries, and visual and verbal explanations of reasoning to help people monitor computer-use agents. A user study examines progress awareness, error traceability, and multitasking across background and foreground interaction.

name: Invisible Ink Threats: Adversarial Goals Behind Legitimate Tasks in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). HITLCUA simulates human participation through an API-simulated user.
summary: Introduces II-Bench for low-harm indirect prompt injections against computer-use agents and HITLCUA for testing them in virtual-machine and web environments with simulated user review.

name: Navigation Alone Is Not Enough: Evaluating Explanatory Assistive UI Agents
notes: Packaged tasks use recorded linear transition graphs. Reported model experiments use a text-input validation subset, so their results are not evidence of screenshot-based navigation performance. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (3.3 Interface states and task annotations; 3.4 Evaluation; 4.1 Models and experimental setup; 5 Discussion).
summary: Introduces NeXUI, an assistive UI-agent benchmark that evaluates navigation together with interface-grounded explanations and user oversight in recorded interface states.

name: Act2Intention: A Benchmark For Developing Active Mobile Agents Through Inferring User Intention from GUI Actions
notes: The benchmark combines real and generated trajectory material. Opportune intervention timing and real-user acceptance are stated limitations. Section 4.2.2 specifies Android emulator instances for generated action trajectories. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (3 Task definition; 4.1 Raw data collection; 4.2 Trajectory construction; 7 Limitations and future directions).
summary: Introduces intention understanding, prediction, and confirmed execution tasks over mobile GUI trajectories, with a proactive agent combining personalized intention models and experience-guided actions.

name: ADeptS-Bench: Measuring the Trustworthiness of Computer Use Agents Across Devices
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates interface-embedded threats and whether computer-use agents seek clarification when mobile or desktop instructions are ambiguous.

name: Are We There Yet? Assessing Computer-Use Agents for Blind Users' Accessible Interaction with Desktop Applications
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: A diary study deploys the screen-reader-accessible OLLA computer-use prototype with blind users across desktop applications. Recorded commands and interaction traces support model comparisons and analysis of grounding, planning, constraint tracking and termination failures.

name: OmegaUse-SOP: SOP Engineering for Professional Computer Use from Human Demonstrations
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: OmegaUse-SOP converts expert GUI demonstrations into configurable procedures and refines them with domain rules and human input. It records, abstracts, grounds and verifies live execution, with a case study of photovoltaic simulation workflows in PVsyst 7.2.

name: ElderBench: Benchmarking Autonomous Mobile Agents for Older Adults
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ElderBench evaluates mobile GUI agents on smartphone requests elicited from older adults, including indirect and underspecified language. Online and offline tests, instruction normalization and linguistic analyses examine how these request patterns contribute to failures.

name: CoArena: Evaluating Computer-Use and Multi-Agent Systems in Real Time
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The five-system example uses 211 illustrative votes.
summary: Introduces CoArena, an evaluation method where user tasks run concurrently in sandboxed desktops and blind pairwise judgments update a public leaderboard.

name: ERPBench: A State-Grounded Evaluation Paradigm for Computer-Use Agents in Enterprise Software
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ERPBench evaluates screenshot-only agents in enterprise software using database values to check the business records produced by their actions. It pairs these state-based checks with a harness for human approval and analyzes cases where visible completion masks incorrect persisted data.

name: The Verifiable Action Card: Trustworthy Human-in-the-Loop Control for Secure Autonomous Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported attack and task outcomes come from a 24-scenario benchmark.
summary: Presents the Verifiable Action Card (VAC), a browser approval mechanism that derives confirmations from pending actions and binds user approval to execution.

name: Task-State Governance: A Virtual Machine for Verifiable and Recoverable GUI Agent Execution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Presents TaskVM, an interface for specifying desired and preserved application state, checking agent actions, and exposing whether changes can be reversed or compensated.

name: What It Is, Not What It Says: Securing Agentic Browsing Interactions with Web Semantics
notes: Evaluation instructs the model to simulate compromise and measures planner outputs and permission appearance. Utility uses plan matching and LLM-judged element suitability; no steps are executed in that assessment. Assumes an honest first party, trusted browser/harness and untampered instrumentation; multi-page and availability attacks are outside scope. Parallel latency reduction is an unimplemented estimate.
summary: Intact records webpage element provenance and capabilities, isolates planning per element, and uses a browser harness to constrain actions and request consent for third-party interactions.

name: PersonaCUABench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents Serving Diverse Personas
notes: Reviewed the complete retained abstract and selected exact-v1 construction, evaluation and limitations sections. Main interactions and satisfaction ratings use LLM-simulated personas; human annotators validate selected outputs. The harness observes page text, with screenshots only for auditing. Results are not evidence about real demographic populations or desktop agents.
summary: PersonaCUABench varies simulated user requests and clarification dialogue over fixed web tasks, comparing task completion with requirement handling and persona-agent satisfaction ratings.

name: SPIDES: Information-Flow Control for Browser Agents
notes: Reviewed the complete abstract and selected v1 threat-model, policy, evaluation and limitations sections. Guarantees assume correct labels/trusted origins and a trusted browser/harness mediating actions; evaluation uses idealized approvals. Origin-level reader sets can miss recipient distinctions within one origin.
summary: SPIDES propagates HTML integrity and confidentiality labels into agent context and mediates browser actions with information-flow policies and approval gates, evaluated in the labeled MicroNet ecosystem.

name: iPrefBench: A User-Centric Benchmark for Personalized Mobile Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its tasks use an interactive simulated user and a constructed activity history.
summary: Introduces iPrefBench, an iOS benchmark for mobile agents that tests when they infer missing user preferences from activity history and when they ask the user.
